subject: Request: backup/log retention exception for EU data — DPA impact
messages:
From: privacyops@fintechco.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: sara.hughes@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary exception to backup purge window for EU scoped logs

Hi Jonas,

Quick note from the FinTechCo PrivacyOps team — as part of our procurement legal review we identified a gap between Redwood's standard 30-day backup purge for ephemeral logs and our internal requirements for fraud investigations (45 days). We're trying to avoid a DPA amendment if possible.

Can Redwood provide either: 1) a documented exception process for extending backup/log retention for a named customer for a limited duration, or 2) a mechanism to export protected logs to our controlled bucket prior to purge? We filed a procurement ticket (PRIV-342) and I've attached a short exemption request template.

Key constraints: EU region data, logs contain pseudonymized tokens but may include transaction IDs, and any change must be auditable.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week.

— PrivacyOps (FinTechCo)
privacyops@fintechco.com
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: privacyops@fintechco.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary exception to backup purge window for EU scoped logs

Hi — thanks for the clear ask and the form. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Marissa (security) to confirm feasibility and audit controls. A couple of initial data points from our side:

- Our default log/ephemeral backup purge window in the eu-west-1 region is 30 days for KV/prefix cache artifacts and 90 days for full system snapshots; however, the 30-day rule applies to high-frequency ephemeral logs we purge nightly.
- We support customer-initiated exports via S3-compatible export jobs; those can be scheduled pre-purge but need a signed retention exception in our system to avoid automated deletion.

Kimberly/Marissa — can you confirm whether we can: (A) issue a time-boxed retention exception tied to FinTechCo (45 days) with an immutable audit trail, and (B) provide a signed export job manifest to their bucket (they request transfer into their EU-controlled bucket) prior to purge? If so we'll put this into the procurement ticket and offer a one-page DPA addendum.

Jonas
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary exception to backup purge window for EU scoped logs

Jonas — thanks. We can support a documented exception but there are legal and subprocessors considerations to call out: 

1) DPA wording: We'll need an addendum stating the duration, data categories, and that the exception is customer-requested and temporary. We'll also include a clause that Redwood remains the data controller/processor (as currently scoped) and that the export destination must meet our minimum security controls (SSE, restricted ACLs).

2) Subprocessors: If the export or temporary retention touches any managed backup vendor (e.g., third-party snapshot storage), we must list the subprocessors and obtain either customer consent or rely on the standard DPA subprocessors list.

3) Logs vs. Backups: We'll define "ephemeral logs" vs "retention backups" explicitly to avoid scope creep — FinTechCo's ask targets ephemeral logs used for investigation, not cold backups.

I've redlined the DPA to add an "Exceptional Retention" section (see attached redline PDF). Marissa, please confirm technical feasibility and auditability (WORM tags, change log).

Kimberly 
Sr. Counsel, Privacy — Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re: Request: temporary exception to backup purge window for EU scoped logs

Quick technical note: we can implement a customer-scoped retention exception flag that alters the nightly purge job for specific prefixes. Implementation details:

- Exception record in our config service (immutable entry with issuer user id, requested retention days, start/end timestamps) — stored in audit-log and surfaced to Console.
- Purge worker will skip prefixes that match the exception record until the exception end timestamp.
- For exports, we support signed export manifests to an external S3 bucket; we will validate bucket region and bucket encryption at time of export.
- We can emit a downloadable audit bundle (JSON lines) for the exception period showing export/purge events.

Caveats: we currently use a managed backup subprocessor for snapshots in some regions — if the requested data touches that pipeline we need to include that subprocessor in the DPA addendum or do a manual export path that avoids the managed vendor. That adds 3–5 business days of ops coordination.

Proposed next step: Jonas, offer FinTechCo a canary exception: 45-day retention for logs scoped to the transaction-* prefix, with an S3 export prior to purge and an auditable exception record. We'll produce the addendum and export instructions; Legal to confirm the DPA text.

— Marissa (Security Engineering)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: privacyops@fintechco.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, sara.hughes@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary exception to backup purge window for EU scoped logs

Hi — quick recap and next steps after internal review:

1) We can offer a time-boxed "Exceptional Retention" for FinTechCo: 45 days for the specified transaction-* log prefix in eu-west-1.
2) We'll create an immutable exception record and surface it in the Console audit tab.
3) Prior to the end of the 45-day window, Redwood will run an export job to FinTechCo's EU S3 bucket (we will validate region and encryption).
4) If export touches our managed backup subprocessor, we'll either include that subprocessor in an addendum or use a manual export path (ops lead time 3–5 business days).

Attached: redwood_dpa_redline_v2.pdf (Kim's suggested addendum text) and the completed exemption form from PrivacyOps. Rishi — can you prepare an updated commercial note offering this as a one-off (no change to standard DPA but addendum + Ops execution) and confirm whether we should propose a minor one-time fee to cover manual export costs?

PrivacyOps — if this approach is acceptable I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff with our ops lead to lock the export window and sign the addendum.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
